record.title: Friedlander–Milnor conjecture for Lie groups
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a Lie group. Regard $BG$ as the classifying space of the underlying discrete topological group, and let $BG^{\rm top}$ be the classifying space with its usual topology. The canonical map

$$
\psi:BG\longrightarrow BG^{\rm top}
$$

is induced by the identity on the underlying group. **Friedlander–Milnor conjecture.** The map $\psi$ induces isomorphisms on homology and cohomology with every finite abelian coefficient group. This is a comparison conjecture between discrete and topological classifying spaces of Lie groups.
record.source_name: Behrooz Mirzaii, “Homology of GL_n over algebraically closed fields”, arXiv:math/0703337 (2007).
record.references:
**3 papers in this index state this conjecture** (1998–2007). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:math/0312408](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0312408), [arXiv:math/9801098](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/9801098).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0703337

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2007).

record.title: The $C^1$ unipotent Jacobian univalence conjecture
record.statement: Let $f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n$ be a $C^1$ map, and let $J(f)$ denote its Jacobian matrix. A matrix is **unipotent** when all its eigenvalues are $1$. **The $C^1$ unipotent Jacobian univalence conjecture.** If $J(f)$ is unipotent, then $f$ is injective. The conjecture is known for $n=2$ and, if established for all $n$, would imply the Jacobian Conjecture. The paper notes that the stronger bijectivity version has no known counterexample.
record.source_name: L. Andrew Campbell, “Unipotent Jacobian Matrices and Univalent Maps”, arXiv:math/9907157 (1999).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/9907157

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 1999).

record.title: The bounded-degree almost sure period two conjecture for majority dynamics
record.statement: Let $G$ be an infinite graph of bounded degree, and choose the initial opinions independently and uniformly from $\{-1,1\}$. Under majority dynamics, each node's opinion almost surely converges to a cycle of period at most two. **Almost sure period two conjecture.** Every bounded-degree graph has the almost sure period two property. The conjecture extends the almost sure period two theorem for unimodular transitive graphs to all bounded-degree graphs. The paper gives an infinite counterexample without bounded degree, while the bounded-degree case is left open.
record.source_name: Itai Benjamini, Siu-On Chan, Ryan O'Donnell, Omer Tamuz and Li-Yang Tan, “Convergence, unanimity and disagreement in majority dynamics on unimodular graphs and random graphs”, arXiv:1405.2486 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1405.2486

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2014).

record.title: The conjecture that the equal-weight subgraph-count property is quasi-random
record.statement: Let $F$ be a graph with $e(F)>1$, and let $m=|F|$. For a graph property $\mathcal P(F;1/m,\dots,1/m)$ and its weaker version $\widetilde\mathcal P(F;1/m,\dots,1/m)$, the source context defines these as properties concerning equal-weight subgraph counts. **Equal-weight subgraph-count conjecture.** Theorem~ holds for any graph $F$ with $e(F)>1$; equivalently, $\mathcal P(F;1/m,\dots,1/m)$ and $\widetilde\mathcal P(F;1/m,\dots,1/m)$ are quasi-random properties for every such graph $F$. The conjecture extends the theorem proved for regular graphs, stars, and disconnected graphs; the only indicated counterexample is $F=K_2$, which has $e(F)=1$.
record.source_name: Svante Janson and Vera T. Sós, “More on quasi-random graphs, subgraph counts and graph limits”, arXiv:1405.6808 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1405.6808

Status: **open** according to the source (as of May 2014). “We leave this (and extensions to $m>3$) as an open problem.”

record.title: Polynomial-time computability of the maximum forcing number for elementary polyomino graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be an **elementary polyomino graph**, meaning that every edge of $G$ lies in some perfect matching.

**Xu et al.'s conjecture.** The maximum forcing number of $G$ can be computed in polynomial time.

The source says that this conjecture can now be confirmed, so the claim is a theorem rather than an open problem.
record.source_name: Heping Zhang and Xiangqian Zhou, “A Maximum Resonant Set of Polyomino Graphs”, arXiv:1411.7126 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1411.7126

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of November 2014); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: The explicit formula conjecture for Farey transfer-operator eigenfunctions
record.statement:
Let $q$ be a parameter and let $\mathbf{E}_{q}(y)$ denote the function introduced through the Farey transfer operators. For the previously considered cases $q=1$ and $q=\frac12$, one has $\mathbf{E}_{1}(y)=\left(\frac{2}{\pi}\right)^{\frac12}y$ and $\mathbf{E}_{1/2}(y)=y^{\frac12}$. **Explicit formula conjecture.** For all $q$,

$$
\mathbf{E}_{q}(y)=\left(\frac{2}{\pi}\right)^{q-\frac12}y^q.
$$

This extends the two explicitly verified cases and predicts a simple closed form for the functions arising from the Farey transfer operators. The supplied text gives no resolution of the assertion.
record.source_name: Claudio Bonanno and Stefano Isola, “Series expansions for Maass forms on the full modular group from the Farey transfer operators”, arXiv:1607.03414 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1607.03414

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2016).

record.title: The bounded cohomology conjecture for smooth projective surfaces
record.statement:
Let $X$ be a smooth projective surface, and let $C$ be a curve on $X$. Write $h^i(\mathcal O_X(C))=\dim H^i(X,\mathcal O_X(C))$. The **bounded cohomology conjecture** asserts that there exists a positive constant $c_X$ such that

$$
h^1(\mathcal O_X(C))\le c_Xh^0(\mathcal O_X(C))
$$

for every curve $C$ on $X$. The conjecture is stronger than the bounded negativity conjecture and is the main conjecture studied in the paper. The source states that it implies bounded negativity, while the cited work disproves it by constructing a counterexample on a surface of general type.
record.source_name: Sichen Li, “Bounding cohomology on a smooth projective surface”, arXiv:1805.10741 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1805.10741

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of May 2018). “In , the authors disproved by giving a counterexample of surface of general type (cf. ).”

record.title: Symmetry conjecture for crossing distributions of restricted permutations
record.statement:
Let $S_n^k$ denote the set of permutations in $S_n$ having the restriction indexed by $k$, and let ${\rm cr}(\sigma)$ be the number of crossings of a permutation $\sigma$. For an indeterminate $q$, define the crossing-distribution polynomial by

$$
\sum_{\sigma \in S_n^k} q^{{\rm cr}(\sigma)}.
$$

**Symmetry conjecture.** For all integers $n$ and $k$ satisfying $1\leq k\leq n$, we have

$$
\sum_{\sigma \in S_n^k} q^{{\rm cr}(\sigma)}=\sum_{\sigma \in S_n^{n+1-k}} q^{{\rm cr}(\sigma)}.
$$

The paper reports verification by computer up to $n=6$; the general identity is presented as a conjecture and no proof or resolution is supplied.
record.source_name: Paul M. Rakotomamonjy and Sandrataniaina R. Andriantsoa, “New combinatorial interpretations of the binomial coefficients”, arXiv:1903.06589 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1903.06589

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2019).

record.title: Higher-order modified Alder conjecture for a=3
record.statement:
Let $q_d^{(a)}(n)$ count partitions of $n$ into parts at least $a$ whose parts differ by at least $d$. For $1\leq b\leq d+2$, let $Q_d^{(b,-)}(n)$ count partitions of $n$ into parts congruent to $\pm b$ modulo $d+3$, excluding the part $d+3-b$, and define

$$
\Delta_d^{(a,b,-)}(n):=q_d^{(a)}(n)-Q_d^{(b,-)}(n),\qquad \Delta_d^{(a,-)}(n):=\Delta_d^{(a,a,-)}(n).
$$

**Higher-order modified Alder conjecture.** For all $d,n\geq 1$,

$$
\Delta_d^{(3,-)}(n)\geq 0.
$$

This is proposed as a generalization of Kang and Park's modified Alder conjecture to higher equal values of $a=b$. The source gives no proof or counterexample, so the assertion remains open.
record.source_name: Adriana L. Duncan, Simran Khunger, Holly Swisher and Ryan Tamura, “Generalizations of Alder's Conjecture via a Conjecture of Kang and Park”, arXiv:2010.08646 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.08646

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2020).

record.title: A hyperbolic distance identity for intersections of lines in the Poincaré disk
record.statement:
Let $a,b,c,d$ be four complex points on the unit circle $S^1$ in this order, with the Euclidean lines $L(a,b)$ and $L(c,d)$ nonparallel. Let $h$ be an arbitrary point on the Euclidean segment $[b,c]$. Define

$$
g={\rm LIS}[a,b,c,d],\qquad j={\rm LIS}[g,h,a,c],\qquad k={\rm LIS}[g,h,b,d],\qquad l={\rm LIS}[g,h,a,d].
$$

Here ${\rm LIS}$ denotes the line-intersection construction used in the paper, and the special case $j=k$ is allowed. **Hyperbolic distance identity.** The hyperbolic distances in the Poincaré disk satisfy

$$
\rho_{\mathbb{B}^2}(h,j)=\rho_{\mathbb{B}^2}(k,l).
$$

This is a metric relation for the line-intersection construction associated with four cyclic points. The supplied text does not establish whether the statement is proved or remains open.
record.source_name: Masayo Fujimura, Oona Rainio and Matti Vuorinen, “Collinearity of points on Poincaré unit disk and Riemann sphere”, arXiv:2212.09037 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.09037

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2022).

record.title: The second-smallest-value conjecture for the function $f$ on finite groups
record.statement: Let $f$ be the function on finite groups studied in the paper, with $f(G)=1$ precisely for cyclic groups. **Second-smallest-value conjecture.** $2$ is the second smallest value of the function $f$. This conjecture is motivated by the preceding lower bounds for non-cyclic groups and has been verified by computer for many classes of finite groups; its general validity remains open.
record.source_name: Georgiana Fasolă and Marius Tărnăuceanu, “On a group-theoretical generalization of the Gauss formula”, arXiv:2212.09055 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.09055

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2022).

record.title: The all-$k$ counterexample conjecture for dijoin additivity
record.statement:
For an integer $k\geq3$, let $T_k$ be a tournament and let $R$ be an oriented graph; $T_k\Rightarrow R$ denotes their dijoin, formed by adding all arcs from $T_k$ to $R$.

**The all-$k$ dijoin counterexample conjecture.** For any $k\geq3$, there is a tournament $T_k$ with $\operatorname{inv}(T_k)=k$ such that

$$
\operatorname{inv}(T_k\Rightarrow R)<k+\operatorname{inv}(R)
$$

for all $R$ with $\operatorname{inv}(R)\geq1$.

The paper proves this statement for every odd integer $k\geq3$ and conjectures that the same phenomenon holds for even integers. Thus the remaining content concerns even $k$.
record.source_name: Guillaume Aubian, Frédéric Havet, Florian Hörsch, Felix Klingelhoefer, Nicolas Nisse, Clément Rambaud and Quentin Vermande, “Problems, proofs, and disproofs on the inversion number”, arXiv:2212.09188 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.09188

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2022).

record.title: Defant's linear-time conjecture for Pop-Stack Sorting on random permutations
record.statement:
Let $D70E_n$ be a uniformly random permutation in the symmetric group $D70E_n$, and let $D43E\operatorname{Pop}$ denote one step of Pop-Stack Sorting, which reverses every maximal decreasing run of a permutation. Write $D43E\operatorname{Id}_n$ for the identity permutation and let $o(1)$ tend to zero as $n\to\infty$. **Defant's conjecture.** Almost surely, Pop-Stack Sorting needs

$$
(1-o(1))n
$$

steps to reach $D43E\operatorname{Id}_n$ from $D70E_n$. This conjecture predicts a linear lower bound, asymptotically matching the trivial upper bound up to a vanishing factor; its resolution concerns the typical running time of Pop-Stack Sorting on a uniformly random permutation.
record.source_name: Lyuben Lichev, “Lower bound on the running time of Pop-Stack Sorting on a random permutation”, arXiv:2212.09316 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.09316

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2022).

record.title: Nonexistence conjecture for {k, k}-equivelar wnp maps
record.statement: Let $K$ be a **wnp map**, meaning a polyhedral map attaining equality in the lower bound $n\geq (k-1)^2$ for an $n$-vertex $\{k,k\}$-equivelar polyhedral map. **Nonexistence conjecture.** There does not exist any $\{k,k\}$-equivelar wnp map for $k\geq 7$. This would extend the known nonexistence for $k=6$, where no 25-vertex $\{6,6\}$-equivelar polyhedral map exists, and would show that the lower bound is never attained for equal face and vertex degrees at least seven.
record.source_name: Basudeb Datta, “A note on the existence of k, k-equivelar polyhedral maps”, arXiv:math/0506618 (2005).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0506618

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2005).

record.title: Fixed point proportion of dynamical exceptional polynomials
record.statement:
1. What can we say about the fixed-point proportion of groups acting on rooted trees?

2. Fixing the tree $T$, can we find a family of groups such that its fixed-point proportion is nonzero and its Hausdorff dimension converges to $1$?

3. What can we say about the fixed-point proportion of Galois groups?

4. What can we say about the fixed-point proportion of $IMG(f)$ of complex rational functions?

5. What can we say about the fixed-point proportion of $IMG(f)$ of complex polynomials that are not dynamically exceptional?
record.source_name: AimPL: Groups of dynamical origin (posed by Santiago Radi)

record.title: How does the group structure of the Brauer group relate to Brauer classes as obstructions to fineness of moduli spaces?
record.statement: How does the group structure of the Brauer group relate to Brauer classes as obstructions to fineness of moduli spaces? Given a K3 surface $X$ and two K3 surfaces $S_1$ and $S_2$ such that $X$ is a moduli space of sheaves on $S_1$ and $S_1$, can we explicitly construct a third K3 surface or variety $Y$ such that $X$ is a moduli space of sheaves on $Y$ and the obstruction class to fineness of this moduli space is the sum of the obstruction classes coming from $S_1$ and $S_2$?
record.source_name: AimPL: Brauer groups and obstruction problems

record.title: Other (problem 3)
record.statement: Consider $\mathbb{C}(u,v)=\mathbb{C}(\mathbb{P}^2)$. Look at the cyclic algebra $A=(u,v)_n$, defined to be $\mathbb{C}(u,v)\langle x,y \rangle/(x^n-u, y^n-v,xy-\zeta yx)$ with $\zeta$ a primitive $n$th root of unity. Does there exist a transcendence degree 1 subfield of $A$ (also a $\mathbb{C}$-subalgebra) which is not rational? Geometrically, can we find a branched cover $S$ of $\mathbb{P}^2$ corresponding to a maximal subfield of the cyclic algebra, which has a rational map to an irrational curve?
record.source_name: AimPL: Brauer groups and obstruction problems

record.title: Other problems (problem 15)
record.statement:
If $X$ is separably rationally connected, there exists $N(\text{dim} X, \text{deg} X, m)$ such that,
for any $p_{1},\cdots, p_{m}\in X(\mathbb{F}_{p})$, there exists a rational curve $C$ defined over $\mathbb{F}_{p^{N}}$ containing all $p_{i}$. (due to Kollar)
Can you do this without lifting the cardinality of field tend to $\infty$?
Let $X$ be a cubic surface over $\mathbb{F}_{q}$.
Can you find a rational curve defined over $\mathbb{F}_{q}$ through each point?
record.source_name: AimPL: Rational subvarieties in positive characteristic

record.title: Modules over the Cox ring (problem 1)
record.source_name: AimPL: Syzygies and mirror symmetry

record.title: Boundedness and moduli theory (problem 5)
record.statement:
Consider $(X,L)\in F_{2d}$, the universal family $\mathcal{X}\overset{\pi}{\longrightarrow}F_{2d}$, and $\mathbb{P}(\pi_*nL)\simeq\mathbb{P}^g$-bundle over $F_{2d}$ with a section $R$.
Can we find a semi-toric compactification $F_{2d} \hookrightarrow \overline{F}^{\mathcal{F}}_{2d}$ and $\overline{\mathcal{X}}$ its universal family with $(\overline{\mathcal{X}},\epsilon R)$ slc stable over $\overline{F}^{\mathcal{F}}_{2d}$?
record.source_name: AimPL: Higher-dimensional log Calabi-Yau pairs

record.title: Orthogonal polynomials (problem 3)
record.source_name: AimPL: Stability and hyperbolicity (posed by P.~Moussa)

record.title: Estimates for $\overline{\partial}$ (problem 5)
record.statement: Let $\Omega$ be a smooth bounded pseudoconvex domain such that for any $0<\eta<1$, there exists a defining function $\rho_{\eta}$ such that $-(-\rho_{\eta})^{\eta}$ is plurisubharmonic on $\Omega$. Note that such an $\eta$ always exists; however, it could be small. Determine minimal assumptions on $\Omega$ to show that $\overline{\partial}$-Neumann operator $N$ (or the Bergman projection operator $\mathbf{B}$) is globally regular. Determine minimal assumptions on $\Omega$ to show existence of a Stein neighborhood basis for the closure. Are there any domains such that $\mathbf{B}$ is globally regular but no such a family of defining functions exists?
record.source_name: AimPL: Cauchy-Riemann equations in several variables (posed by Harrington)

record.title: Normal Forms (problem 1)
record.statement: Let $C$ be a class of hypersurfaces defined by a finite order condition. A normal form is a subclass $C_0$ where normal representatives are determined up to a finite dimensional group. For example, for Levi non-degenerate hypersurfaces there is the Chern-Moser normal form and for finite type hypersurfaces in $\mathbb{C}^2$ Kollar presented a normal form. Can you find a class where it can be proved that there is no convergent normal form?
record.source_name: AimPL: Cauchy-Riemann equations in several variables (posed by Zaitsev)

record.title: Spectrum of $\overline{\partial}$-Neumann Laplacian (problem 4)
record.statement: Let $\phi:\mathbb{C}^n\to\mathbb{R}$ be a $C^2$ plurisubharmonic function. Determine the relation between the eigenvalues of the complex Hesssian of $\phi$ and the compactness of the $\overline{\partial}$-Neumann operator on $L^2_{(0,q)}(\mathbb{C}^n,e^{-\phi})$. See for $n=1$. Determine the relation between the spectrum of the complex Laplacian $\Box_{\phi}$ and the weight function $\phi$. In particular, understand the bottom (infimum) of the essential spectrum.
record.source_name: AimPL: Cauchy-Riemann equations in several variables (posed by Haslinger)

record.title: Spectral problems (problem 2)
record.statement:
Consider the domains

$$
\Omega_k = \left\{ (z,w) \in \mathbb{C}^{n+1} \colon \mathrm{Im}(w) < \lvert z\rvert^{2k} \right\}
$$

and

$$
U_k = \left\{ (z,w) \in \mathbb{C}^{n+1} \colon \mathrm{Im}(w) < \sum_{j=1}^n \lvert z\rvert^{2k} \right\}.
$$

(a) Can one compute the spectrum of the Kohn Laplacian on $(0,1)$-forms in either case?

(b) Can one distinguish $\Omega_k$ from $U_k$ using the spectrum?
record.source_name: AimPL: Analysis and geometry on pseudohermitian manifolds (posed by J. D'Angelo and S. Fu)

record.title: Homogeneisation of the Steklov-Neumann problem
record.statement:
Let $\Omega$ be a domain in $\mathbb R^2$ and fix a fraction of the perimeter. Consider partitions of its boundary into $\Gamma = \Gamma_N \cup \Gamma_S$. Put Neumann boundary conditions on $\Gamma_N$ and Steklov on $\Gamma_S$. 

a) How should one separate the boundary to maximise the first non-zero eigenvalue?

b) What happens under homogeneisation?

c) What happens if one instead puts a weight on the boundary, i.e. amongst all functions $\rho$ on the boundary with fixed integal and value between $0$ and $1$, find the $\rho$ that optimises $\sigma_1$ in the eigenvalue problem

$$
\begin{cases} \Delta u = 0 \\ \frac{\partial u }{\partial n} = \sigma \rho u \end{cases}.
$$
record.source_name: AimPL: Steklov eigenproblems (posed by Nilima Nigam)

record.title: Problems on Holomorphic Function Spaces (problem 6)
record.source_name: AimPL: Problems on holomorphic function spaces and complex dynamics

record.title: Problem List (problem 14)
record.statement: For positive semidefinite (PSD) zero forcing consider the minimum PSD propagation time $\text{pt}_+(G):= \min\{\text{propagation times given a minimum PSD zero forcing set}\}$ and the maximum PSD propagation time $\text{PT}_+(G):= \max\{\text{propagation times given a minimum PSD zero forcing set}\}$. If $\text{pt}_+ (G) \le k \le \text{PT}_+(G)$ is there a minimum PSD zero forcing set with propagation time $k$? This is not true for standard zero forcing, skew zero forcing, directed zero forcing, loop zero forcing or power domination propagation time.
record.source_name: AimPL: Zero forcing and its applications

record.title: 2-lift of Ramanujan graph
record.statement:
Is a random 2-lift of a Ramanujan graph also Ramanujan (or nearly) with constant probability? More precisely, let $G$ be a $d$-regular Ramanujan graph with adjacency matrix $A$. Construct the matrix $S$ by

$$
S_{ij} = \left\{\begin{array}{cl} 0 & \text{if } A_{ij} = 0 \\ \text{randomly } \pm 1 & \text{if } A_{ij} = 1. \end{array}\right.
$$

Is the spectral norm of $S$ less than $2\sqrt{d-1} + \epsilon$ with constant probability?
record.source_name: AimPL: Connecting communities via the block model (posed by Nikhil Srivastava)

record.title: Distribution of Intersection Numbers of Undirected Graphs
record.statement: Given an undirected graph $G$, a clique of $G$ is an induced subgraph of $G$ that is complete (that is, any two distinct vetices are adjacent). An edge clique cover is a set of cliques covering all vertices of $G$. The intersection number of a graph $G$ is the number of cliques in a minimum edge-clique cover. Question: What is the distribution of these intersection numbers? If one were to make a histogram of all undirected graphs on $n$ vertices, what is the distribution of these intersection numbers?
record.source_name: AimPL: Gems of combinatorics (posed by Alex Markham)

record.title: Parameter determination for post-quantum hash functions
record.statement: In the design of the hash function one has control over two parameters; the dimension of the special linear group considered, and the characteristic of the underlying field. We would like to determine appropriate choices for both via two branches of cryptanalysis: first, by analysis of the multivariate system implied by long matrix products; and second by direct analysis of group-theoretic properties. We should also study the impact of the partial homomorphicity exhibited by the scheme.
record.source_name: AimPL: Post-quantum group-based cryptography

record.title: Open problems (problem 5)
record.statement:
Let $X$ be a complex symplectic algebraic manifold and $G$ a complex reductive group with $G\curvearrowright X$ in a Hamiltonian fashion, $\mu:X\rightarrow \mathfrak{g}^{\ast}$ a moment map and $Y=X//_{\lambda}G=\mu^{-1}(\lambda)/G$. 
 
Find examples where: 

i) $Y$ is an algebraic completely integrable Hamiltonian system.

ii) $Y\ncong \mathcal{M^{\ast}}(\Sigma)$ (some moduli of tame/wild Higgs on decorated surface)
record.source_name: AimPL: Spectral data for Higgs bundles (posed by Hoskins)

record.title: Nonlinear representation theory
record.statement:
Suppose we define an abstract notion of "wild nonabelian Hodge structure", consisting of a hyperkahler manifold with its various algebraic structures, such that it is a wild Hitchin moduli space for some choice of a group, an irregular curve and residue data. The choice of such a realisation of the abstract space can be viewed as a "representation" or "realisation" of the space. Study this representation theory.

Here we are viewing these moduli spaces as global/nonlinear analogues of algebraic groups (as the Riemann--Hilbert problem suggests).

For example, take one simple example (such as the $D_4$ Hitchin space, the Painleve VI space, $GL_2$ with four simple poles on $P^1$), of complex dimension $2$ and find all the possible representations of this space.
record.source_name: AimPL: Spectral data for Higgs bundles (posed by Boalch)

record.title: Geometric flows (problem 3)
record.statement:
Consider the flow of inverse Hermitian metrics on a compact complex manifold:

$$
\frac \partial {\partial t} g^{j \overline k} = g^{m \overline n} \partial_m \partial_{\overline n} g^{j \overline k} - \partial_m g^{j \overline k} \partial_{\overline n} g^{m \overline k}.
$$

One has short time existence, and it is known that at the maximal time of existence

$$
| \mathrm{Rm}^{\mathcal{Ch}} | + |T| + |\nabla T| \to \infty.
$$

Can this be improved? Can one find analogues of Perelman's $\mathcal F$ and $\mathcal W$ functionals?
record.source_name: AimPL: Nonlinear PDEs in real and complex geometry (posed by Yuri Ustinovskiy)

record.title: For geodesic flows on non-compact metric spaces, can the variational principle have an extremal measure and metric?
record.statement:
For geodesic flows on non-compact metric spaces, can the variational principle have an extremal measure and metric? That is, if $\mathcal M_f$ is the set of $f$-invariant probability measures on $X$, $\mathcal D_X$ is the space of distances on $X$ inducing the same topology, $h_d(f) = \displaystyle \sup_{K \subset X} h_d(f,K)$ where the supremum is taken over the topological entropy of compact subsets $K$ with respect to the metric $d$, and:

$$
h_{\operatorname{Borel}}(f) & = & \sup_{\mu \in \mathcal M_f} h_\mu(f) \\ 
h_{\operatorname{top}}(f) & = & \inf_{d \in \mathcal D_X} h_{d}(f)
$$

The Borel and topological entropies were shown to coincide in for locally compact spaces. Under what conditions can one find a metric $d$ and measure $\mu$ which realize the common value?
record.source_name: AimPL: Equilibrium states for dynamical systems arising from geometry (posed by Jerome Buzzi and Todd Fisher)

record.title: Rigidity (problem 6)
record.statement:
In L. Lovasz’s paper ["Flats in Matroids and geometric graphs”], he considers the dimension of $span(F\cap h)$, where $F$ is a family of linear subspaces of $R^d$, $h$ is a subspace of codimension 1 in $\mathbb{R}^d$, and $F\cap h:=\{f\cap h \mid f\in F\}$. He proves that this dimension can be expressed as a certain minimum over all the partitions of the elements of $F$, given that $h$ satisfies a certain "general position” assumption. The questions are:

(i) Can the general position assumption in Lovasz’s theorem be relaxed?

(ii) Can one find a formula (in whatever terms) that applies to subspaces $h$ that are not necessarily in general position?
record.source_name: AimPL: Rigidity and flexibility of microstructures (posed by Orit Raz)

record.title: Gradient Estimate
record.statement:
Consider the equation

$$
F[\lambda[u]]=\psi,
$$

where $\omega_{0},\omega_{X}$ are nonnegative Hermitian $(1,1)$-forms
and $\lambda[u]$ are the eigenvalues of $\omega_{0}+\sqrt{-1}\partial\overline{\partial}u$
with respect to $\omega_{X}$. Assume the $C$-subsolution condition
holds, and that $F$ is concave. Is it possible to prove effective
estimates (not through a contradiction argument) of the form

$$
\sup_{X}|\nabla u|\leq C(\omega_{0},\omega_{X},\psi,F)?
$$

For example, can one prove this using maximum principle techniques? 

Blocki did this for the complex Monge-Ampere equation using maximum
principle techniques, but so far there is no known direct proof in
the case of the $\sigma_{k}$ equations. It is also known in the case
of deformed Hermitian-Yang-Mills.
record.source_name: AimPL: PDE methods in complex geometry (posed by Bin Guo)

record.title: The Problems (problem 6)
record.statement:
Let $X$ be a Hilbert modular surface over ${\\mathbb{Q}}$. All of the Tate classes that arise from modular curves on $X$ are defined over ${\\mathbb{Q}}^{ab}$; however, there also exist Tate classes which are algebraic, but not defined over ${\\mathbb{Q}}^{ab}$. (In fact, they are defined over dihedral extensions of ${\\mathbb{Q}}$.) We know the algebraicity of these classes, but do not know specific representatives.

Comments:

1. One possible suggestion for such representatives could be non-congruence curves on $X$. (D. Ramakrishnan)

2. If we can find representatives, we can intersect them with the modular curves: this may be a way to find interesting non-Heegner points on the modular curves. (D. Ramakrishnan)
record.source_name: AimPL: The Tate Conjecture (posed by D. Ramakrishnan)

record.title: The Problems (problem 18)
record.statement: Let $E$ be an elliptic curve over ${\\mathbb{Q}}$ with CM by $K$ and with associated Hecke character $\chi$. Then $\chi^2$ is associated to a modular form of weight 3 appearing in $H^2(\mathcal E)$, $\mathcal E\to X$ for a modular curve $X$ (whose level is the norm of the conductor of $\chi^2$ times the discriminant of $K$). The Tate and Hodge Conjectures predict the existence of a correspondence $E\times E\to \mathcal E$ because the same motive appears in $H^2$ of both sides. Can we exhibit this correspondence explicitly?
record.source_name: AimPL: The Tate Conjecture (posed by D. Ramakrishnan)

record.title: Moduli height
record.statement:
Let $X$ be a quasi-projective variety and $G$ a group action on $X$. Let $Y=X//G$ be a geometric quotient of $X$ by $G$. Is $h_Y(x) \asymp \min_{g \in G} h_X(gx)$? (ample heights)

 In particular, fix an embedding $M_d \subset \mathbb{P}^M$. Then define a height $h_M:M_d \to {\\mathbb{R}}$ using the embedding. Is this height function comparable to the minimum height of the maps in the class in $\mathop{Rat}_d$?
record.source_name: AimPL: Postcritically finite maps in complex and arithmetic dynamics

record.title: Can one find a version of the recipe using asymmetric approximate functional equations, giving a “robust” version of the calculations?
record.statement:
Can one find a version of the recipe using asymmetric approximate functional equations, giving a “robust” version of the calculations? Similarly, can one apply the Conrey-Keating method using two asymmetric Dirichlet polynomials

$$
\sum_{m\leq X} \frac{\tau_A(m)}{m^s} \ \ \ \ \ \ \text{and} \ \ \ \ \ \ 
\sum_{n\leq Y} \frac{\tau_B(n)}{n^{1-s}}
$$

to get the same answer as before, i.e. when $X=Y$?

record.title: Complexity (problem 1)
record.statement:
Let $K$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0, and let $G$ be an ordered divisible group. Consider the Hahn field, defined as follows:

$$
K((G)) = \left\{\sum_{g\in S}a_g t^g \mid S\subseteq G \text{ well-ordered}, a_g\in K\right\}
$$

If $K$ and $G$ are computable and $f\in K((G))[X]$, how complex is it to determine a root of $f$?
At each step, the procedure should produce the next term in a root of $f$, based on the $a_g$ in the input coefficients of $f$. For each step $\alpha$, how many jumps over these coefficients are needed to do step $\alpha$?
record.source_name: AimPL: Definability and decidability problems in number theory (posed by Julia Knight)

record.title: Problems related to Xiao-Zhu (problem 1)
record.statement: Consider Xiao-Zhu specialized to Tate classes associated to Hilbert modular forms at an inert prime. In the generic case, i.e. when the Satake parameters are different, then there is a 2-dimensional space of Tate classes, and Xiao-Zhu produce a 2-dimensional space of cycles. In the nongeneric case the dimension of Tate classes is $4$, and Xiao-Zhu produce only 1 cycle. Can you find extra cycles when the Satake parameters are equal? More generally, in non-generic cases of Xiao-Zhu, can you construct the missing cycles?

record.title: Similar to Kudla program, we could also define a generating series of (derived) complex multiplication cycles on Shimura varieties and conjecture its modularity.
record.statement: Similar to Kudla program, we could also define a generating series of (derived) complex multiplication cycles on Shimura varieties and conjecture its modularity. Is it possible to compute arithmetic intersection of the generating series with special divisors / Hodge bundle and prove its numerical modularity when the Shimura variety has low dimension e.g. on Siegel threefold or Hilbert modular surface?

record.title: Computing Fourier coefficients from $L$-values
record.statement:
Let $d$ be a positive integer and let $F$ be a Siegel modular form with Fourier coefficients $a(F)$. In many cases, we know the (generalized) B\"{o}cherer conjecture:

$$
\left \lvert \sum_{S \in \mathrm{Cl}_d} a(F, S) \Lambda(S) \right \rvert^2 = L\big(\pi_F \times \theta_\Lambda, \frac{1}{2}\big) = L\big(\mathrm{BC}_{K/\mathbb{Q}} (\pi_F) \times \Lambda, \frac{1}{2}\big).
$$

Knowing this equality and values of $L(\pi_F \times \theta_\Lambda, \frac{1}{2})$ for many $\Lambda$, can we compute the Fourier coefficients $a(F, S)$?
record.source_name: AimPL: Analytic, arithmetic, and geometric aspects of automorphic forms (posed by Manami Roy)

record.title: There were several questions proposed around this, including What should the predicted values of … be?
record.statement:

* What is the "shape" of the set $U$ that one should take? In the usual Manin conjecture, one expects that $U$ can be taken to be the complement of a thin set.

* Can one compute asymptotics for $N_{X,\mathscr L}(U,B;d)$ if $X=\mathbb P^2_{\mathbb Q}$ and $d=3$, for some choices of $\mathscr L$?

record.title: Examples of MCG-finite irreducible representations of surface groups not arising from abelian varieties
record.statement:
Can we find an examples of an irreducible representation $\rho: \pi_1(\Sigma_{g,n}) \to {\\textrm{GL}}_r(\mathbb{C})$ with finite orbit under $\mathrm{Mod}(\Sigma_{g,n})$ that do not arise from families of abelian varieties? 

We say that a representation “arises from a family of abelian varieties” if there exists a complex structure on $S = \Sigma_{g,n}$ such that there is an Zariski open $U \subset S$ and a family of abelian varities $A \to U$ such that the representation restricted to $U$ is a subquotient of the Gauss-Manin local system of $A \to U$.
record.source_name: AimPL: Motives and mapping class groups

record.title: Moments of derivatives
record.statement:
What do the methods for computing moments of L function give if one tries to
compute moments of derivatives.
Even in the random matrix theory setting computing the distribution of
derivatives is difficult.
What can recent methods tell us about the distribution of values of derivatives
of $L$ functions?
This structure is related to the Painlev\'e V equation, and the moment (for
finite $n$) is a polynomial in $N$, the size of the random matrix.
Also, they correspond to solutions for Painlev\'e III as $n \to \infty$.
record.source_name: AimPL: Moments in families of L-functions over function fields (posed by Jon Keating)
